newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan harvest forges ahead on good weather.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan harvest forges ahead on good weather.

text.p: Saskatchewan's harvest surged to 78 percent complete from 55 percent the previous week, aided by good weather conditions, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its crop report for the week ended October 14.
For all crops, harvest was 78 percent complete versus 99 percent a year ago and 95 percent over the five-year average.

Of the 75 percent of the spring wheat harvested, 57 percent was expected to grade No1 Canada Western Red Spring, 22 percent as No2 CWRS, 19 percent as No3 CWRS and two percent as feed wheat. Sprouting, bleaching and lodging all caused problems in the harvest.

Southern Saskatchewan saw an average of less than 1.0 mm of rain but many standing crops remained flattened by heavy snow from early October. Sprouting and bleaching continued to damage crops. Rain on Thanksgiving Monday stopped harvest.
Central Saskatchewan saw an average of two mm of rain. Sprouting, bleaching and frost continued to be sources of damage. Allan reported hail damage.
Northern Saskatchewan saw an average 4.0 mm of rain. Sprouting and bleaching damaged crops.
